questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Fudan offers a wider range of English-Language courses than other Chinese Universities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Highly rewarding, both academically and personally.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: This ranges widely between departments and from bachelor to masters. Would say it is generally very difficult if you need complete reassurance, as information can change from day to day and the sources of information vary widely.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A series of buddies were assigned on top of student coordinators, department coordinators and international student coordinators. They each give information ranging from Chinese immigration to logistics of campus life. Some task like physical printing is difficult to understand, but everything is going to be fine, if you actively seek help when you need it and join various WeChat (social media) group chats. Even higher levels of international student coordinators are willing to help in most hours, even during late evening.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are three levels of student housing: supplementary dorms, Shared main building dorms and Main building dorms, ranging in price from 2200 dkk to 4500 dkk per month. Rent is paid for the whole semester upon arrival.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: close to none. The canteens are close and offer a wide range of options, including "Western" food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
You won't be able to apply for student dorms until just before the exchange, so keep that in mind. If you want to make sure you get a spot at the more covetted supplementary student dorms, you can stay up all night at wait for application to open. But it should be fine, if you apply the following day. But it is first come first served. 
Many foreigners have rented apartments or shared with other students. If you plan to do this, I recommend deciding in advance, as you will pay the whole rent for student dorms upon arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Student dorms are on campus, and although they don't have a curfew, you need to pass a guarded gate, and visiters must register as your guests. Visitors, be that nightly or otherwise, may or may not be allowed, but there is no actual enforcement. However, if you plan to have many or regular visitors outside of the university, you should consider renting an apartment.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very confusing. Masters students are more likely to get courses they want, and professors are often willing to allow student to participate in any class regardless of their level or department, if you ask nicely and clear it with the administration.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Available quite late online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Many people have varying information and it changes. Rely on your own department and the international student coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 10/10! If some course seems unavailable, make sure to contact the professor responsible for the course. It is likely that they will alow you to enter.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try as many classes as possible. You have plenty of time to get to know campus, other students and the city, so for the first two weeks, just try out a lot of classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only had classes outside my own field, but professors and students were very accomodating, and the level was not unreachable with some diligence.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some departments also offer PhD level courses. I highly recommend these if you enjoy seminar style classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Evaluation is also based on active participation and regular presentations. These presentations are individual and vary in difficulty. You will need to make a lot of PPTs but they don't have to be particularly fancy.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: You will probably start taking taxis a lot more, as they are very cheap and public tranportation stops around midnight.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Bring your tennis racket and your swim shorts. Fudan has a wide range of sports facilities. If you do engage in sports, I recoomend bringing equipment and trying out for the teams here. Buying equipment here is quite cheap also.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: most.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: swimming. There is a 50 meter pool, which is not too crowded. You can also try to find one of the sunday running clubs - or start your own.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips. Visiting nearby cities is cheap and easy. And do go to the rural areas. Try to bring a friend who knows just a bit of Chinese.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. But I recommend bringing a good phone.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask if they want to have coffee or something. If you do sports, try out for the club in the start of the semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: language

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendlyness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: bring an extra credit card, go to the city as often as you can, and try not to buy too much crap on Taobao

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's really easy to buy a cheap scooter, so if thats interesting, make sure you have a good inurance before you go. You can get the cheap ones for 1500, but some cost as little as 400 for the whole semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Overall rewarding. A lot of good friends, experiences and academic insights

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: time difference to denmark

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
